key_insight: The paper argues that browser agents fail mainly because they lack the right priors for decision-making under partial information, not because they can’t execute low-level actions. It shows that human browsing traces already contain reusable “skills” that can be distilled into scalable browser behavior cloning.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of training browser agents to perform complex web tasks reliably across diverse, real-world workflows without requiring exhaustive hand-coded rules or task-specific supervision.
method: Collect large-scale human browser interaction traces as a source of implicit skills.
Use skill distillation to extract reusable decision-making priors from these traces.
Train behavior cloning models to imitate human browsing patterns and improve agent performance under incomplete information.
impact: This matters because it turns everyday human web activity into a scalable training signal for browser automation. For AI/ML practitioners, it suggests a practical path to building more capable web agents with less manual engineering and better generalization across tasks.
visual_elements: Workflow pipeline: human browsing traces -> skill distillation -> browser agent training

paper_title: Scalable Behaviour Cloning on Browser Using via Skill Distillation
paper_authors: Kaisen Yang, Zheng Jiang, Yuzhao Peng, Houde Qian, Boshi Zhang
